Cross-cutting observation: The multi-store fix surfaced a structural pattern that all future MCP tool handler authors must follow — Constraint 86 in constraints.md codifies it. The most important deferred item is createWorkPackage write routing (D-1): it currently uses resolveMultiStoreLedgerRoot for read-path resolution but should use resolveStoreForWrite for write-path routing, meaning WP creation in a non-default store still silently lands in the default store. This is the only remaining multi-store gap after this project. CTX regeneration (node scripts/cli.js ctx-generate) is needed before the next planning cycle.

outcome_summary: Fixed multi-store mode failures across the entire AI Insights codebase by extracting a shared store-resolution utility (store-resolution.ts / store_resolution.py) and applying it uniformly to all 18 MCP tool handlers, the GUI HTTP layer and auto-archive service, the standalone-import tool, and the orchestrator's path helpers. The approach followed a sequential WP chain: shared utility first (WP-001), then independent surfaces in parallel (WP-002 GUI, WP-003 orchestrator), then dependent handler migration (WP-004, WP-005), and finally manifest documentation (WP-006). 47 new tests were added across both TypeScript (4,010 total pass) and Python (1,131 non-live-API pass) suites; no regressions were introduced. The one remaining multi-store gap — createWorkPackage write routing — was deferred as a known follow-on item.
project_summary: This project fixes multi-store mode failures across the entire codebase by extracting a shared store-resolution utility and applying it to all 16 broken MCP tool handlers, the GUI HTTP layer, auto-archive service, standalone-import tool, and orchestrator path helpers. Without this fix, projects in non-default stores silently fail with file-not-found errors on read operations and phantom directory creation on write operations.
